knowledge: Python provides built-in data types such as int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, set, and dictionary. Different data types are used to represent different kinds of values.
A list is an ordered and mutable collection in Python. Lists can contain multiple values and support indexing, slicing, insertion, deletion, and iteration.
A tuple is an ordered immutable collection. Tuples support indexing and iteration but their elements cannot normally be changed after creation.
A dictionary stores data as key-value pairs. Dictionaries are mutable and provide efficient lookup by key.
A set is an unordered collection of unique elements. Sets support operations such as union, intersection, difference, and membership testing.
Python functions are reusable blocks of code. Functions can accept positional arguments, keyword arguments, default arguments, and variable-length arguments.
Lambda functions are anonymous functions written using the lambda keyword. They are commonly used for short operations with functions such as map, filter, and sorted.
Decorators are functions that modify or extend the behavior of another function without directly changing its source code. They are commonly implemented using nested functions and functools.wraps.
An iterator produces values one at a time using the iterator protocol. Generators provide a convenient way to create iterators using yield. Generators evaluate lazily and can reduce memory usage.
List comprehensions provide a concise way to create lists by applying an expression to elements of an iterable, optionally using a condition.
Python handles runtime errors using try, except, else, and finally blocks. Custom exceptions can be created by defining classes derived from Exception.
Python provides file handling through the open function. Files can be opened in modes such as read, write, and append. The with statement is commonly used to manage file resources safely.
Python supports object-oriented programming using classes and objects. Classes can contain attributes and methods and support concepts such as inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism.
Inheritance allows a class to derive behavior and attributes from another class. Python supports single, multiple, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance.
Polymorphism allows the same interface or operation to work with different object types. Python commonly achieves this through duck typing and method overriding.
Python modules organize reusable code into files, while packages organize multiple modules into a structured directory. Python supports importing functions, classes, and modules.
Context managers manage resources using the with statement. They commonly implement __enter__ and __exit__ methods and can also be created using contextlib.
Python manages memory automatically using mechanisms including reference counting and garbage collection. Objects are allocated in a private heap managed by the Python memory manager.
A closure occurs when an inner function remembers and accesses variables from its enclosing scope even after the outer function has completed execution.
Python supports multithreading through the threading module. Threads can be useful for I/O-bound tasks, while CPU-bound execution is affected by the Global Interpreter Lock in standard CPython.
Python asynchronous programming uses async and await with an event loop to handle cooperative concurrent tasks, especially I/O-bound operations.
Caching stores previously computed results so repeated operations can avoid unnecessary computation. Memoization commonly uses function arguments as cache keys and stores corresponding results.
Generators can use yield to produce values lazily. Advanced generators can receive values through send(), handle exceptions with throw(), and terminate with return.
